# NKE — Quantitative Fundamental Attractiveness Report
**Decision date: 2026-06-12 | Latest filing: Q3 FY2026 (period_end 2026-02-28)**

---

## 1. Revenue, Earnings & Margin Trajectory

NKE's latest quarter shows a business under clear earnings pressure. Q3 FY2026 revenue of $11.28B is essentially flat YoY (vs. $11.27B in Q3 FY2025, +0.1%), but profitability has collapsed: EPS diluted fell to $0.35 from $0.54 (−35.2% YoY), net income dropped to $520M from $794M (−34.5% YoY), and operating income compressed to $650M from $844M (−23.0% YoY). On a QoQ basis the deterioration is equally severe — revenue declined −9.2% from Q2's $12.43B, EPS fell −34.0% from $0.53, and operating income dropped −35.0% from $999M.

The margin erosion is broad-based. Gross margin compressed to 40.1% ($4.53B GP on $11.28B rev) versus 41.4% ($4.67B on $11.27B) in the year-ago quarter. Operating margin fell to 5.8% from 7.5% in Q3 FY2025 and cratered from 11.5% in Q2 FY2026's $1.42B predecessor context (Q2 FY2025 showed operating income of $1.42B on $12.35B, implying ~11.5% margins). Net margin compressed to 4.6% from 7.0%. This is not a single-quarter anomaly — Q2 FY2026 net income was $792M (6.4% margin) and Q1 was $727M (6.2% margin), a three-quarter slide from double-digit operating margins in earlier periods.

The trajectory of the five reported quarters tells the story: from Q2 FY2024 ($0.78 EPS) through Q3 FY2025 ($0.54), Q1 FY2026 ($0.49), Q2 FY2026 ($0.53), and now Q3 FY2026 ($0.35). Earnings have roughly halved in two years on essentially flat top-line. Note: TTM is incomplete (fiscal gap prevents a contiguous trailing twelve months) — I am not constructing a TTM sum.

## 2. Cash Generation & Balance-Sheet Resilience

Cash generation has deteriorated alongside earnings. Q3 FY2026 operating cash flow was $430M, down −76.0% YoY from $1.79B and −25.7% QoQ from $579M. While Q3 FY2025's $1.79B OCF included notable working-capital benefits, the current quarter's $430M against $520M net income (OCF/NI = 0.83x) suggests limited cash conversion headroom. Free cash flow data is unavailable.

The balance sheet provides modest support. Total equity stands at $14.09B (total assets $37.06B, total liabilities $22.97B). The equity-to-asset ratio is 38%, and the company carries no apparent debt-service stress from the balance sheet alone. However, balance sheet data contains a reporting anomaly for prior quarters (negative total liabilities values), so absolute leverage cannot be precisely triangulated across all periods. The latest quarter's equity base ($14.09B) is essentially unchanged from Q3 FY2025 ($14.01B), indicating no significant capital destruction but also no meaningful growth through retained earnings given the weak profit trajectory.

## 3. Valuation versus Own History

This is where the disconnect is most concerning. The latest P/E diluted is 30.3x with an earnings yield of 3.3%. Over the past year, P/E has ranged from 19.5x to 38.9x, and the current reading sits in the upper half of that range. Yet this elevated multiple is being paid on collapsing earnings — NKE's P/E expanded from ~20.6x in June 2025 (when net margin was 9.4% and ROE was 32.2%) to 30.3x today (net margin 4.8%, ROE 16.0%). The market has not re-rated cheaply into the downturn; rather, the multiple has stretched as the denominator has shrunk, leaving the stock expensive relative to actual earnings power.

P/B has contracted meaningfully from 8.2x (August 2025) to 4.8x, now at the floor of its 365-day range (4.4–8.4x). This reflects price decline more than book value growth. P/S at 1.46x is modest for a branded consumer company but offers no margin of safety given the margin erosion. The earnings yield of 3.3% trades below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.45%, implying the equity risk premium is negative — the market is pricing either a recovery in earnings or a premium that current fundamentals do not justify.

## 4. Price Context versus Fundamental Path

The stock has declined in a near-unbroken sequence: $74.25 → $63.33 → $54.13 → $45.96, three consecutive quarterly declines of −14.5%, −14.7%, and −15.1%. The 365-day range of $41.35–$80.17 places the current $45.96 near the bottom quartile. Price has correctly anticipated the fundamental deterioration. However, the stock has already declined ~43% from peak, which is substantial. The question is whether the fundamental bottom is in sight — and the sequential margin compression in the latest quarter argues it may not be.

## 5. Macro & Sentiment Overlays

Macro conditions offer limited support. The 10-year Treasury yield at 4.45% is elevated and rising (up ~22bp over 90 days), compressing the relative attractiveness of equities with low earnings yields. Oil at $91.58/bbl adds cost pressure for a manufacturing-heavy consumer discretionary name. The VIX at 19.44 is moderate but ticked higher from sub-16 levels in late May. The yield curve (10Y-2Y at 0.40%) remains positive but narrow.

News sentiment is persistently negative: 90-day mean score of −0.396 across 60 scored articles, with dominant readings of −1.0 on many days. The emotional tone reinforces the quantitative deterioration but should not be overweighted.

## 6. Strongest Quantitative Upside & Downside

**Upside:** P/B at 4.8x is at the trough of its 365-day range; if NKE stabilizes margins at even mid-single-digit levels and the brand holds, a reversion to the 6–7x P/B range implies 25–45% upside in equity value. The $14B equity base and 40% gross margins indicate durable pricing power that could reassert.

**Downside:** The P/E of 30.3x prices in a recovery that the trajectory does not yet support. If margins remain at 4.8% net / 5.8% operating and revenue stays flat, the stock could de-rate toward its lower P/E band (~19.5x), implying ~35% further downside. The negative earnings yield spread versus the risk-free rate is a structural headwind. Cash generation at $430M/quarter with unclear free cash flow leaves limited dividend/buyback flexibility if the downturn persists.

## 7. Provisional Conclusion

NKE presents as fundamentally unattractive at current levels. The core problem is a widening gap between valuation and earnings quality: a 30x P/E on 4.8% net margins and 3.3% earnings yield is untenable without a credible earnings recovery — and the latest quarter shows continued sequential deterioration, not stabilization. The balance sheet provides a floor but not a thesis. Margins are compressing, cash generation is weakening, and the stock is not cheap on any earnings-based metric relative to its own history. Until there is a quarter showing margin stabilization or revenue acceleration, the fundamental case is negative. Price has declined substantially, but valuation remains elevated relative to actual business performance.

# NKE — Qualitative Franchise & Narrative Assessment

**Decision date: 2026-06-12**

---

## 1. Business / Franchise Read

Nike remains the world's most recognized and valuable sportswear brand, with ~$46 billion in annual revenue, presence in 190+ countries, and an estimated 27% share of the global sportswear market. The business model is asset-light: Nike designs, markets, and outsources nearly all manufacturing to ~660 contract factories (concentrated in Vietnam, Indonesia, and China), then sells through two channels — Nike Direct (owned stores and apps) and wholesale partners. Footwear accounts for roughly two-thirds of NIKE Brand revenue; Converse is a smaller, shrinking subsidiary ($1.7B in FY2025, down 19%).

The franchise itself — brand equity, innovation pipeline, global distribution, cultural relevance — is structurally intact. What broke was execution. Under former CEO John Donahoe, Nike over-rotated toward direct-to-consumer, pulling products from wholesale partners and training consumers to expect discounts. The result: FY2025 revenue fell 10% to $46.3 billion and net income dropped 44% to $3.2 billion, with diluted EPS declining to $2.16 (down 42%). The brand's pricing power eroded, competitors (On, Hoka, Adidas) captured shelf space Nike vacated, and inventory bloated.

Returning CEO Elliott Hill launched the "Win Now" plan: rebuild wholesale relationships, clear stale inventory, refocus on performance sport (running, basketball, training), reset digital away from perpetual promotions, and streamline the organization. Early FY2026 results show wholesale revenue rising 8% (Q2 FY2026) while Nike Direct declined 8% — a deliberate rebalancing. In Q3 FY2026, Nike Running surged more than 20%, and management highlighted the "Sport Offense" strategy driving athlete-led innovation. The model still throws off meaningful cash: Nike holds $8.06B in cash and short-term investments against $8.03B in debt, has raised its dividend for 24 consecutive years (current yield ~3.8%), and maintains an $18 billion buyback authorization (currently paused as a prudent capital-allocation decision during the turnaround).

The key structural question is whether Hill can restore pricing power and cultural relevance quickly enough to offset a multi-year competitive head start given to rivals. The consensus view: turnaround benefits will not meaningfully land until FY2027, with projected revenue growth of only ~3% versus an industry average of ~6%.

## 2. Recent Developments (Dated)

- **2026-06-11 (Benzinga):** RBC Capital Markets downgraded Nike, cutting its price target from $70 to $50, citing slower-than-expected revenue growth and delayed turnaround benefits. The analyst projects revenue growth of just 3% versus the industry average of 6%, with turnaround benefits materializing in 2027 rather than 2026.
- **2026-06-11 (Newsline / StockAnalysis):** Nike reported Q1 FY2026 EPS of $0.35, beating consensus of $0.28 by 22.89%. Revenue figures were not fully disclosed in the available data. The stock declined 1.55% despite the beat, signaling investor skepticism about top-line momentum.
- **2026-06-03 (Motley Fool):** Nike shares have declined 68% over the past five years. Analysts forecast only 1.7% annual revenue growth through 2028.
- **Recent (StockAnalysis, ~late May/early June):** JPMorgan downgraded Nike to Underweight with a $40 price target, estimating the company could face a $1 billion headwind in China and that "Win Now" decisions made in 2026 will hurt profits.
- **Recent (StockAnalysis):** Nike is expecting a ~$986 million tariff refund as an "unplanned benefit," announced alongside FY2026 Q3/full-year results.
- **Recent (StockAnalysis):** Nike's China business has shrunk ~30% since 2021, with annual revenue at its lowest level in eight years.
- **2026-06-23 (GuruFocus):** Nike announced a planned CFO transition.
- **FY2025 structural data (businessmodelanalyst.com):** Tariffs will cost roughly $1 billion in gross incremental expense in FY2026. Nike is shifting U.S.-bound footwear sourcing from China (from ~16% to "high single-digit range") and raising some prices selectively. Demand creation (marketing) spending rose 15% in Q4 FY2025 to ~$1.3B, signaling management is investing through the downturn rather than retrenching.
- **Full-year FY2026 consensus (StockAnalysis/Yahoo):** EPS of ~$1.49 (down ~31% YoY), revenue of ~$46.36 billion (essentially flat). Next earnings release: June 30, 2026.

## 3. Material Risks and Offsets

**Risks:**
- **Turnaround timeline uncertainty.** Consensus and multiple analysts expect the EPS trough to land in FY2026 (~$1.50), with recovery to ~$3.00 by FY2028. Any slippage in wholesale rebuild, China stabilization, or margin recovery extends the timeline and compresses returns.
- **China structural weakness.** Revenue down ~30% since 2021; management describes the problem as a "cultural lag" requiring multi-quarter rebuild, not a quick pricing fix. JPMorgan estimates a $1B headwind.
- **Tariff and supply-chain exposure.** Sourcing concentrated in Vietnam (~51% of footwear) and Indonesia; ~$1B gross FY2026 tariff cost, partially mitigated by sourcing shifts and the ~$986M refund. The tariff refund is one-time and does not address structural cost inflation.
- **Competitive share loss.** On, Hoka, and Adidas gained wholesale shelf space during Nike's DTC pivot. Reclaiming that position requires sustained product innovation and retailer relationship repair.
- **Legal exposure.** A proposed class action lawsuit alleges Nike raised prices to offset tariffs and failed to issue refunds after tariffs were struck down. Outcome uncertain but adds reputational and cash-flow risk.
- **Valuation not obviously cheap.** At ~$41-43 per share, one analyst pegs FY27E P/E at 23.4x — rich for a consumer non-durable with no demonstrated top-line growth since FY22. The Zacks consensus analyst price target is ~$50.87.
- **CFO transition** announced for June 23, 2026, adding leadership continuity risk during the turnaround.

**Offsets:**
- **Durable brand moat.** Nike's brand equity, cultural relevance (Jordan: $7.27B in revenue), and innovation pipeline remain best-in-class. Over 2 million consumers signed up for Nike Mind notifications, demonstrating continued consumer pull.
- **Balance sheet strength.** Net cash position ($8.06B cash vs. $8.03B debt), 259% current ratio, and 24 consecutive years of dividend increases provide financial resilience through the trough.
- **Management credibility.** Hill is a 32-year Nike veteran who previously ran the commercial business; his "Win Now" plan is showing early wholesale traction and he is investing in marketing ($4.7B, up 9% YoY) rather than cutting brand spend.
- **Running category momentum.** Nike Running surged 20%+ in Q3 FY2026, and scalable innovation platforms (Nike Mind, Aero-FIT, Liquid Air Max) are being launched.
- **EPS beat signals operational discipline.** Q1 FY2026 EPS of $0.35 beat consensus of $0.28 by 22.89%, suggesting margin management may be ahead of expectations even if revenue remains soft.
- **Tariff refund.** The ~$986M unplanned benefit, while non-recurring, provides near-term cash-flow support.

## 4. Qualitative Assessment

**Assessment: Cautiously Negative / Deep-Value Watch**

Nike is a world-class franchise in the middle of a genuine operational reset. The brand moat, balance sheet, and asset-light model are structurally sound. The "Win Now" plan under Elliott Hill is directionally correct — wholesale rebuild, sport-first innovation, marketing reinvestment — and early results (wholesale +8%, Running +20%+, EPS beat) suggest the medicine is working.

However, the turnaround is early and multi-dimensional. Revenue is essentially flat, EPS is declining (~$1.49 consensus for FY2026 vs. $2.16 in FY2025), China is a multi-quarter rebuild, tariffs are a ~$1B structural cost drag, and competitive share loss to On/Hoka/Adidas will take time to reverse. Multiple sell-side analysts have recently cut price targets or downgraded the stock. The next earnings catalyst (June 30, 2026) will be critical for establishing whether wholesale momentum is accelerating or stalling.

The qualitative narrative does not yet support fundamental attractiveness at current levels for a new position — the risk/reward is asymmetric but skewed toward patience. The franchise quality is undeniable; the question is execution timing, and the evidence says the trough (both in earnings and likely in sentiment) has not yet been confirmed. This is a name to monitor for inflection evidence in upcoming quarters, not one where current qualitative data justifies conviction today.

Pillar 1 (fundamentals): Earnings have collapsed — Q3 FY2026 EPS of $0.35 is down 35% YoY and represents a continued sequential slide from $0.78 (Q2 FY2024) through $0.54, $0.49, $0.53, and now $0.35. Cash generation has deteriorated sharply: OCF of $430M is down 76% YoY from $1.79B. Revenue is essentially flat at $11.28B. The trajectory is unambiguously negative with no stabilization visible. Pillar 2 (valuation): At a P/E of 30.3x with a 3.3% earnings yield — below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.45% — the stock is expensive relative to its own history (was 20.6x a year ago when margins were double today's levels). The market is pricing a recovery that the data does not yet support. P/B at 4.8x is at the trough of its range, but this reflects price decline, not value creation. Pillar 3 (near-term catalyst): The next earnings release (June 30, 2026) is a potential catalyst, but multiple sell-side analysts have recently downgraded or cut targets (RBC to $50, JPMorgan to Underweight with $40 PT), consensus FY2026 EPS is ~$1.49 (down 31% YoY), and turnaround benefits are not expected until FY2027. The near-term catalyst skews negative — the risk of further disappointment in the upcoming print is elevated given China weakness (~30% decline since 2021), ~$1B tariff headwind, and competitive share loss to On/Hoka/Adidas. The franchise quality is real (27% global share, Jordan $7.27B revenue, 24 consecutive dividend increases), but a world-class brand with deteriorating execution, collapsing margins, and an expensive multiple is not an attractive investment at this juncture.
